results.content:
### PandaDoc

PandaDoc offers a free e-signature tier with unlimited signatures, which sounds incredible. The catch: the free plan lacks templates, content libraries, custom branding, and analytics. The Essentials plan at $35/month per user adds those features. For a small team of three, that's $1,260/year. PandaDoc is really a document automation platform that happens to include e-signatures, so you're paying for proposal-building features even if you just need contracts signed.

### Watch for Hidden Costs [...] Third, what's included at your price tier? Audit trails, mobile signing, PDF delivery, and multi-party support should be standard at every price point, including free. If a vendor locks audit trails behind a $65/month enterprise plan, they're monetizing a basic legal requirement. That tells you something about their pricing philosophy.

## The Pricing Model That Makes the Most Sense in 2026

The e-signature industry is moving away from per-envelope and per-user models because buyers have realized those structures don't align with how businesses actually use the tools. You don't charge a printer per page in 2026. You shouldn't pay per signature either. [...] ### Send Unlimited Contracts for a Fixed Price

Zignt gives you everything this guide recommends at a price that doesn't scale with your growth. Reusable templates, unique signing links that work like payment links (create once, share with anyone), multi-party signing, automatic PDF delivery, and complete audit trails. Your signers never need an account. Plans start free, with the Professional tier at $12/month for unlimited signatures. No per-envelope fees, no per-user multipliers.
